summary:
TERRASCAN is an AI-powered geospatial platform that identifies Earth locations resembling potential Moon base sites and Mars landing environments. It uses terrain, geological and environmental analysis to support planetary exploration research.

The platform includes modules for planetary exploration, analog discovery, Earth location mapping, environmental comparison, mission suitability analysis and reporting.

It uses React, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS and MapLibre for the frontend, with Python and FastAPI for the backend. Geospatial and AI technologies include GeoPandas, Rasterio, NumPy, Pandas and Scikit-learn, with SQLite for database management. NASA, ESA and USGS are the intended scientific data sources.

The analysis workflow includes data acquisition, preprocessing, feature extraction, similarity analysis and visualization. Key comparison factors include slope, elevation, surface roughness, thermal conditions and geology.

Potential Earth analog locations include the Atacama Desert, McMurdo Dry Valleys, Death Valley, Haughton Crater and Icelandic volcanic landscapes.

Future development will focus on integrating verified scientific datasets, improving similarity analysis, validating machine learning models and enhancing terrain assessment.

TERRASCAN aims to connect Earth-based geospatial intelligence with planetary exploration by helping researchers study terrestrial environments that share characteristics with the Moon and Mars.
details:
TERRASCAN: AI-Powered Planetary Analog Intelligence Platform

1. Project Overview

TERRASCAN is an AI-powered geospatial intelligence platform designed to identify and evaluate locations on Earth that resemble potential permanent lunar base sites and Mars landing environments. The project addresses an important challenge in future space exploration: finding suitable terrestrial environments that can serve as analogues for studying extraterrestrial terrain, geological conditions, and environmental characteristics.

Earth contains several extreme environments, including deserts, volcanic landscapes, polar regions, and impact craters, that share certain characteristics with the Moon and Mars. TERRASCAN aims to analyze these environments using geospatial data, terrain analysis, environmental indicators, and AI-assisted comparison techniques.

The platform brings together planetary exploration data and Earth observation information to help researchers explore potential analog locations, compare environmental characteristics, and assess their relevance to future space missions.

2. Problem Statement

Selecting suitable locations for permanent lunar bases and Mars landing missions requires extensive analysis of terrain, geological characteristics, environmental conditions, and surface properties.

However, identifying Earth locations that resemble these extraterrestrial environments involves working with multiple scientific datasets and complex geospatial information. Manually comparing these datasets is time-consuming and makes large-scale analysis difficult.

TERRASCAN aims to address this challenge by providing a centralized platform for exploring, analyzing, and comparing terrestrial environments with selected lunar and Martian reference conditions.

3. Project Objectives

The primary objectives of TERRASCAN are:

  • Identify Earth locations that resemble selected lunar and Martian environments.
  • Analyze terrain characteristics, including slope, elevation, and surface roughness.
  • Evaluate thermal, geological, and environmental similarities.
  • Integrate scientific datasets from organizations such as NASA, ESA, and USGS.
  • Apply geospatial processing and machine learning techniques to support location analysis.
  • Provide interactive maps and visual comparisons of potential analog locations.
  • Support research and preliminary mission-site suitability studies.

4. Key Features and Modules

Overview Dashboard: Provides a centralized view of the platform, its analytical capabilities, and important project information.

Planetary Explorer: Allows users to explore Moon and Mars environments and understand the reference conditions used for terrestrial comparisons.

Analog Discovery: Identifies potential Earth locations based on selected planetary environmental and terrain characteristics.

Earth Locations: Provides information about candidate terrestrial environments, including their geographical and physical characteristics.

Comparison Module: Supports comparisons between selected Earth locations and planetary reference environments.

Mission Suitability Analysis: Organizes mission-relevant characteristics to help assess the potential usefulness of different terrestrial analog environments.

Reports Module: Provides a framework for presenting analytical findings, comparisons, and location assessments.

5. Technology Stack

The project follows a modular frontend and backend architecture.

Frontend:

  • React
  • TypeScript
  • Vite
  • Tailwind CSS
  • MapLibre
  • Recharts

Backend:

  • Python
  • FastAPI

Geospatial Processing and Analysis:

  • GeoPandas
  • Rasterio
  • NumPy
  • Pandas
  • Scikit-learn

Database:

  • SQLite

Scientific Data Sources:

  • NASA
  • European Space Agency (ESA)
  • United States Geological Survey (USGS)

6. Analytical Methodology

TERRASCAN follows a structured analytical workflow:

  1. Data Acquisition: Collect relevant planetary and terrestrial geospatial datasets.
  2. Data Preprocessing: Validate datasets, handle missing information, and standardize spatial references and data formats.
  3. Feature Extraction: Extract relevant characteristics such as elevation, slope, roughness, thermal conditions, and geological information.
  4. Similarity Analysis: Compare terrestrial environmental characteristics against selected lunar and Martian reference conditions.
  5. Candidate Evaluation: Organize potential analog locations based on their measured similarities and available evidence.
  6. Visualization: Present geographical information, comparisons, and analytical findings through interactive interfaces.

The analytical framework is designed to distinguish similarity scores from data completeness and confidence, ensuring that users can understand the reliability and limitations of individual comparisons.

7. Potential Earth Analog Locations

The initial candidate environments considered by the project include:

  • Atacama Desert, Chile: An extremely arid environment relevant to studying Mars-like conditions.
  • McMurdo Dry Valleys, Antarctica: A cold, dry environment useful for investigating certain Martian analog conditions.
  • Death Valley, USA: An environment with distinctive desert terrain and geological characteristics.
  • Haughton Crater, Canada: An impact crater environment relevant to planetary geology research.
  • Icelandic Volcanic Landscapes: Volcanic terrain that provides opportunities for studying geological analogues.

These locations are candidate research environments, not scientifically validated equivalents of specific lunar or Martian landing sites.

8. Development and Implementation

TERRASCAN has been developed through a staged implementation process. The project architecture, frontend foundation, interactive mapping components, planetary exploration interface, and several supporting application modules have been addressed during development.

The initial implementation includes candidate-location visualization and the structural foundations for geospatial analysis and planetary comparisons.

Further validation is required to establish reliable real-world data integration, scientifically calibrated similarity rankings, complete frontend-backend functionality, and machine learning performance using representative scientific datasets.

9. Applications and Significance

TERRASCAN can support:

  • Planetary science and geological research.
  • Lunar and Martian analog environment studies.
  • Preliminary extraterrestrial mission-site research.
  • Geospatial intelligence and environmental analysis.
  • Educational demonstrations of planetary exploration technologies.
  • Research into terrestrial environments that simulate selected extraterrestrial conditions.

By combining geospatial technologies with AI-assisted analytical methods, the project provides a foundation for exploring the relationship between Earth's extreme environments and the challenges of future planetary exploration.

10. Future Scope

Future development will focus on integrating verified scientific datasets, improving geospatial processing capabilities, validating similarity calculations, developing reliable machine learning models, and expanding interactive visualization features.

Additional improvements may include advanced terrain classification, more detailed environmental comparisons, mission-specific evaluation criteria, and automated scientific report generation.

11. Conclusion

TERRASCAN aims to bridge terrestrial geospatial analysis and planetary exploration research through an integrated AI-powered platform. By identifying and evaluating Earth environments that share selected characteristics with the Moon and Mars, it provides a framework for studying planetary analogues and supporting preliminary research for future space exploration missions.

The long-term vision is to develop TERRASCAN into a reliable, transparent, and extensible planetary analog intelligence platform that makes complex environmental comparisons more accessible to researchers, students, and space exploration enthusiasts.
